messages.subject: slightly off-topic : stan_trace plotting question
parts:
This isn't really a stan question, but it did
arise with one of the rstan plotting functions
and I haven't been able to solve it; so if there's
an easy solution, I'd very much like to know.

Suppose you're plotting the traces of a stanfit object
using stan_trace. You experiment a bit, and find
a layout that's pleasing, say nrow=6, ncol=2 per page.
You can now arrange a loop that plots params 1:12, then
13:24 etc.

The problem comes at the last page. Suppose you have
just two parameters left over. These two will fill
the entire page, and are quite out of scale with the
rest. Is there some easy way to avoid this? One
possibility might be to fill the rest of
the positions with empty plots (10, in my example)
but I don't know how to do this.




Thanks for any suggestions!

Maybe the marrangeGrob()function in the gridExtra package would help? It definitely works with the ggplot objects returned by stan_trace, I'm just not sure which exact options you'll need to specify to get the layout you want, but it should be possible. 

Jonah

messages.author: 30b37db3d992e3df
messages.subject: Re: slightly off-topic : stan_trace plotting question
parts:
Thanks! This does just what I wanted. For those wanting a quick template, here's what I did, where mod is a stanfit object:

library(gridextra)

    p<-lapply(1:length(names(mod)), function(x) stan_trace(mod, pars=names(mod)[x]))
    m<-marrangeGrob(p,nrow=6,ncol=2)
    print(m)

you may want to add   top=""  to the call to marrange: this omits the
"page m of n" headers. And if you are using a large-ish number of rows you might want to try

rstan_ggtheme_options(axis.title=element_text(size=10))

which reduces the font size of the parameter identifiers on the left.


Thanks again!
